newsitem.title: USA: Calif. utilities seek shorter restructuring period.
newsitem.headline: Calif. utilities seek shorter restructuring period.

text.p: Edison International's Southern California Edison Co and Pacific Gas and Electric Co filed jointly with regulators to shorten to three years the state's transition to a deregulated electric industry, the utilities said Tuesday.
But another key goal of the filing is to establish a "real-life" test during the initial year of open access, said Edison spokesman Gary Schoonyan.
"We think it is best that the people in charge of consumer protection and reliability be able to adjust the rate of phase-in based on how things go in the first year."
Under recently-passed state legislation, open access for a segment of each electricity customer class, including residential and small business users, would start in 1998 and be finished in 2001.
The California Public Utilities Commission had set a five-year period to phase in direct access for all electricity consumers by 2003.

But Edison and PG&E are seeking to allow customers representing 1,800 megawatts of usage to choose their own supplier starting in 1998. More users would be phased in by 1999 and all customers would be allowed open access by 2000.
The 1,800 MW would include customers of Edison and PG&E customers as well as Enova Corp's subsidiary San Diego Gas and Electric Co, the state's other major investor-owned utility.

PG&E said the "aggressive schedule" proposed to the CPUC would be affected only by technical capabilities of an independent system operator, customer protection requirements and the utilities' system capabilities.
